name: Blog
description: A blog from Markdown posts: renders each post, the index and an RSS feed with its own theme, then publishes them as one Ravi Pages route.

help.usage: ravi blog build --posts <folder> [--title <t>] [--description <d>] [--author <a>] [--lang pt-BR] [--url <site url>] [--drafts true]
help.summary: Render the site from the Markdown posts in <folder> and return the files, without publishing.

sections.title: Posts
lines: One .md file per post. Optional front matter between --- lines: title, date (YYYY-MM-DD), description, tags (comma-separated), slug, draft (true).
An optional site.json in the folder sets title, description, author, lang, url and footer; flags win over it.
The folder must be inside the working directory. Raw HTML in posts is shown as text, and links may only be http(s), mailto or relative.

help.summary: Render the site and publish it as one route of the project's Ravi Page (default /blog).
examples: ravi apps run blog publish --execute -- --posts posts --title "Notas"

sections.title: Rules
lines: Publishing is a write: the router asks for --execute.
Every publish renders every post again, so the index and the feed always match the folder.
The route keeps the project's visibility (private by default); only the operator makes it public, with ravi pages visibility.

help.summary: List the published routes; posts are the ones under /blog/.
Read a published post or the index back, to edit it or match its style.
